text:
acme_integration: Hi @sam_support — we started seeing intermittent JSON parse failures from structured_output=true in prod. ~5% of responses fail with `Unexpected end of JSON input at position 142`.

acme_integration: Example request (we're streaming):
```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-v1","stream":true,"structured_output":true,"prompt":"generate menu as JSON"}'
```

acme_integration: And a raw chunk sequence we captured (lines are the SSE/data chunks we reassembled):
```
data: {"id":"r1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"menu\": [ {\"name\": \"Margherita \"}\n"}}}
data: {"id":"r1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"🍕\"},"finish_reason":null}]}
data: [DONE]
```

acme_integration: The client JSON.parse fails because the pizza emoji appears to split across chunk boundary, and a literal newline ends up inside the JSON string. We've tried increasing client buffer size but it's flaky. Also seeing CRLF vs LF differences when the caller is on Windows.

sam_support: Thanks for the repro, sending to eng. Quick questions: which SDK/version, streaming transport (SSE/websocket), and which region? Any sample of the exact parser error and full chunk bytes (hex) would help.

acme_integration: SDK: node@3.2.1, using SSE; region: us-west-2. Parser error: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)` from our service logs. We attached a small pcap of the SSE payload (I pasted the decoded bytes above).

anya_engineer: @acme_integration thanks — two hypotheses: 1) multi-byte UTF-8 (emoji/supplementary planes) is being split across chunk boundaries and our client-side reassembly is dropping/transforming bytes; 2) our streaming runtime is emitting raw newlines in the middle of a JSON string (e.g., unescaped CR or LF) when generating formatted text, which breaks strict parsers.

anya_engineer: Immediate mitigation: set `stream=false` (non-streaming) or post-process the received stream before JSON.parse: replace literal CRLF/newline inside string regions with escaped `\\n` and coalesce incomplete UTF-8 sequences. Example quick hack in Node: 
```
let buf = Buffer.concat(receivedChunks);
// naive fix: ensure UTF-8 integrity then stringify
buf = buf.toString('utf8');
buf = buf.replace(/\r\n/g, '\\n');
const obj = JSON.parse(buf);
```

sam_support: Also to reduce retries & cost while we investigate: we can apply a small token credit to the workspace. @acme_integration do you want 5k token credit while we triage?

acme_integration: Yes please, that would help as we've had to retry multiple times. Thanks.

anya_engineer: Repro steps I ran locally to mimic the issue: 1) send streaming request with small chunk_size config (we used internal low chunk emitter) 2) generate emoji-heavy output & a few literal newlines inside JSON values 3) assert that client reassembly yields invalid JSON. I could reproduce with a toy model that emits a 4-byte emoji split across two chunks.

anya_engineer: Action: escalating to eng-runtime. Created ticket INC-2026-142 and attached the pcap + chunk logs. Assigning to @mike_sre for infra-level investigation (possible SSE emitter bug or encoder layer).

mike_sre: Acked — I'll take it. First steps: 1) verify our streaming encoder always emits valid UTF-8 boundaries (no half-surrogate writes), 2) ensure we escape internal newlines in structured JSON mode (i.e., the runtime should emit `\\n` not literal LF inside JSON strings), 3) add unit tests for surrogate pair boundary cases and CRLF normalization.

mike_sre: Can @acme_integration share an anonymized sample ID we can replay on staging? If not, we'll try to reproduce with the pcap.

acme_integration: I'll DM a small sample id. Also note this started after we flipped `structured_output` to strict mode (schema enforcement). Non-strict mode returns text we post-process and we've had fewer failures.

sam_support: Credit applied: 5000 tokens. I've also flagged this as P1 due to production parsing failures causing user-facing errors. I'll keep you updated. :eyes:

anya_engineer: Temporary workaround for other customers: prefer `stream=false` for strict JSON consumers, or use a tolerant parser that can stitch surrogate halves and normalize CRLF. We're going to prioritize a runtime patch that guarantees emitted JSON is byte-safe across chunk boundaries.

mike_sre: ETA for a hotfix: investigating now, aiming for a staged fix in the next 24-48h with a canary rollout. Will post test build and request a repro run.

acme_integration: Thanks everyone — will try non-streaming and DM sample. Appreciate the token credit and fast triage.
